newsitem.title: UK: UK motor insurers face losses in 1996 - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK motor insurers face losses in 1996 - survey.

text.p: The UK motor insurance market is expected to post losses in 1996 according to the sixth annual Bacon & Woodrow survey.

While the market enjoyed healthy profits in 1995, they were down from the previous two years' levels and, said Bacon & Woodrow, the survey indicates that the market is at the lower end of the insurance cycle.

Large insurers were unable to translate economies of scale into better profitability than top performing small firms with Eagle Star,Sun Alliance and Commercial Union among those faring less well in 1995.
Norwich Union and Guardian Royal Exchange improved their ranking in the industry, though Guardian did suffer an absolute drop in profitability levels.

The survey also indicated that when premiums do start to rise, new entrants such as banks and building societies will find it easier to enter the market with the strength of their retail brand having a huge say in their success.

"Retail banks will have new policy acquisition costs of about half those without a consumer brand, and the strength of the brand will allow higher pricing," said David Campbell, a partner at Bacon & Woodrow.
